family_basis: Select James Glasgow (Glasgow-1238), the father recorded with Elizabath/Elizabeth Tait at Stichill, as Robert Glasgow’s possible working father, at 34%. The couple’s maintained marriage citation is dated 25 January 1740; their David and James children are indexed in June 1744 and July 1746. Robert’s estimated 1745 birth fits that family generation and could fall between those events; it is not a dated baptism. Stichill and Eccles/Leitholm belong to the same small Borders district, and the later Swinton entry attributed to the James/Tait couple offers a further local comparison. Robert’s earlier son James supplies a modest naming clue consistent with this father; a common forename cannot establish paternity. The combination favours this existing, record-defined family over the catalogue’s distant Kirknewton candidates, whose apparent proximity came from mapping Leitholm to South Leith. No inspected record names Robert as James’s son.
limitations: This is a preferred, revisable hypothesis, with 34% subjective confidence, not a measured probability or a confident connection. Robert’s 1745 birth and 8 August 1800 death each have zero attached sources on the inspected FamilySearch tree. Neither date establishes an age or place of birth. The local 1745 estimate is retained unchanged. FamilySearch attaches John Glasgow (1720–1785, GFNP-FS8) and Agnes Spark (1722–deceased, K8CD-HCW) as parents; retain that alternative without treating a contributed tree as documentary proof. The evidential basis of that parent attachment has not yet been reviewed. Do not equate that John with the much older John Glasgow-1057, husband of Agnes Spark-330, from the matching names alone. James’s brother John Glasgow-1444, christened at Stichill in 1708, is another compatible local father-generation alternative with no presently inspected Robert link. An unrecorded local father or another kinship degree remains possible. The Swinton/1740 couple continuity and Robert’s own early life need testing. Elizabeth Tait is not selected as Robert’s mother: her marriage and maternity of other children do not identify his mother. Robert is not merged with an earlier child, and James’s existing older ancestry retains its own uncertainty.
